title: Widespread Protests Ignite Debate on Civil Liberties, Supreme Court Intervenes Amidst Detentions and Celebrity Outcry
summary: Recent events have seen prominent figures like Dhruv Rathee and leaders of the CJP protest detailing alleged detentions without legal access, sparking a nationwide conversation on civil liberties. The Supreme Court has intervened, issuing directives against illegal detentions and disruptions of public services, while celebrity reactions remain sharply divided. Beyond the protests, other significant news includes a tragic car accident involving a minor, an emergency flight landing due to a power bank fire, and various developments in the entertainment world, highlighting a dynamic period of social and technological discourse.
article:
**Dhruv Rathee Details Detention Ordeal, Denies Undertaking**

Prominent YouTuber Dhruv Rathee recently disclosed a harrowing account of his detention, alleging that he was held for approximately 20 hours without access to his phone or legal counsel. Rathee claimed plainclothes policemen entered his home, pushed his mother aside, and dragged him to multiple police stations and locations. He asserted his Indian citizenship by displaying his passport in a video, addressing initial skepticism about its authenticity.

Following his release, reports circulated that Gurugram Police had released him on an undertaking that he would not participate in future protests. Rathee vehemently denied these claims, labeling them "fake news" and clarifying via tweet that he "did not sign any bond. I did not sign any undertaking. I did not sign any conditions for release." He also confirmed that he participated in the protests in an individual capacity, not as an affiliate of the CJP (Citizens for Justice and Peace).

**CJP Leaders Allege Phone Seizure, Police Dispute Claims**

Leaders of the CJP also faced detention, with Sourav Das alleging that his phones were seized without any seizure memo. Das expressed concern that the police might have tampered with or planted evidence on his devices, citing similar incidents with other activists.

Delhi Police, however, issued a statement confirming the preventive arrest of Abhijeet Ashutosh and Sourav, stating they were produced before an SCM Court and released on a bail bond of ₹50,000 for maintaining peace and good behavior for one year. Abhijeet Deep, another CJP leader, explicitly denied signing any such bond, stating on Twitter, "we have not signed any such bond that we will not be able to protest. We will hit the streets again." CJP leaders also announced plans to visit Parliament Street Police Station to demand a date for a peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar.

A related controversy arose concerning the passing of Abhijeet Deep's grandmother. Rumors spread that Delhi Police had not informed him, but the police released a video purporting to show them informing Abhijeet and offering assistance for travel to the funeral. Abhijeet countered this, stating he was refused permission to speak to his cousin, whose number he didn't know, for just a few minutes on his phone. He also questioned the police's motive for instructing him at 3:30 AM to call his father, who had just lost his mother, to inform him about potential jail time.

**Supreme Court Upholds Rights to Peaceful Protest**

Amidst widespread detentions of protesters, the Supreme Court issued a clear directive against illegal detentions of peaceful, unarmed individuals, emphasizing that such actions must be in accordance with the law. The court also mandated that metro and railway services, as well as internet connectivity, should remain undisturbed, ensuring normal operations during protests.

**CJI's "Fly" Remark Sparks Online Meme**

A remark by the Chief Justice of India (CJI) regarding the heavy police security at the CJP protest, "A hammer should not be used to kill a fly," quickly gained traction. This led to the creation of an online page named "Yaar Makkhi Janata Party," which garnered over 3 lakh followers within a day, turning the comment into a viral meme.

**Bollywood Divided on Protest Stance**

The CJP protests elicited varied reactions from the entertainment industry. Photos and clips of actor Imran Khan casually posing for selfies with policemen went viral. Rajendranath Judshi was seen engaging with protesters, while Vijay Verma posted "Saving Private Gyan," seemingly referencing Gyanesh Kumar. Uma Qureshi stressed the fundamental right to peaceful protest in a democracy, and Sonakshi Sinha shared excerpts from the Constitution on citizens' rights.

Neeshu Tiwari critically questioned the presence of "goons" in orange scarves alongside police, assaulting individuals without authority. In contrast, Kangana Ranaut stated that ordinary citizens would now confront "anti-national forces." Actress Tansha Mukherjee criticized "well-educated elitist Hindus" for supporting "factions from America and Germany who want to destroy a country," calling it "wrong" to be labeled a "blind devotee" for supporting the government.

**Entertainment Industry Updates**

In other news, **Nakul Dhull** entered the Bigg Boss house as a wildcard, initially feigning to be a Chemistry and Physics teacher. He later advised fellow contestant Scout to maintain distance from Love Gill. **Purva Jha's** new YouTube video was blocked after a copyright claim, leading him to express frustration over the platform's system. Actor **Eijaz Khan** defensively responded to criticism over intimate scenes in a musical shot, questioning why other actors can perform similar acts without religious backlash, stating, "Allah Taala has said that do not call the song Kanha. My Allah will settle my account. Who are you to judge me?" Fans of **Toby Maguire** expressed disappointment after news broke that the OG Spider-Man actor officiated the wedding of his ex-wife and her new husband. In a heartwarming story, a dedicated **GTA 6 fan** from Brazil received a surprise package from Rockstar Games after emailing them about buying their game with his first paycheck.

**Public Safety and Negligence Incidents**

A tragic incident in Kochi saw a 19-year-old run over three people with his gifted Mini Cooper, reportedly at a speed of 125 km/h. Eyewitnesses claimed the driver, allegedly under the influence of alcohol, callously stated, "my father will handle this case." The local MLA has promised justice for the victims.

In a miraculous escape captured on CCTV, a man on a bike in an unspecified location survived a high-speed car collision, being thrown into the air for a fraction of a second but landing unharmed, while his bike was completely destroyed.

An Indigo flight from Delhi to Chennai made an emergency landing in Hyderabad after a power bank exploded and caught fire inside the cabin. Crew members extinguished the fire, and all passengers were safely evacuated, with an alternate aircraft arranged for their onward journey.

In Pune, a shocking incident of negligence occurred when a patient fell out of a moving ambulance onto the road. While preliminary investigations indicated no serious injuries, questions are being raised about the ambulance's security measures and the presence of medical staff.

Finally, during a heavy earthquake in Panama, CCTV footage showed several individuals risking their lives to save liquor bottles from falling shelves, highlighting unusual priorities amidst a natural disaster.
